Subject: DPF addendum and a few missing artifacts

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call earlier — AmeliaCare legal has one follow-up: we need a brief addendum to the DPF materials you shared that ties the DPA Annex language to the operational artifacts. Specifically we need:  

- A simple entity map showing which Redwood entities process Ameliacare data and at what stage (ingestion, inference, logging/metrics).
- A network diagram showing egress/ingress boundaries and which third-party clouds are involved.
- A draft DPA Annex highlighting the sections you see as most relevant to cross-border transfers and subprocessors.

Can you provide these as PDFs/diagrams by EOD tomorrow? Also procurement (Tom Richards) may be looped in for contract redlines — I cc'd him on the thread in case we need to sync.

Appreciate the quick turn — this is gating our security review.

Best,
Sophie Lane
Head of Security & Privacy
AmeliaCare

Sophie — thanks for the clear list. See the attached preliminary artifacts:  

- redwood_dpf_entity_map.pdf (maps processors/roles and data lifecycle stages)
- network-traffic-diagram.png (high-level egress/ingress + region hops)
- dpa-annex-draft.docx (annotated draft that calls out transfer mechanisms and fallback language)

Quick notes:  
- The entity map includes our hosted service (Redwood Hosted API), Dedicated pools (customer-dedicated GPUs), and the Private deployment offering — each row notes whether data is transient or persisted for metrics.
- The network diagram shows where we route inference traffic, the optional VPC peering paths for Private customers, and where we currently use cloud storage for model artifacts (can be swapped by request).
- The DPA annex draft includes suggested language for DPF fallback (e.g., SCC-equivalent safeguards, contractual assurances). Karthik has marked a couple of legal clauses that might need tightening for regulated healthcare customers.

We plan to produce a control-mapping CSV that ties the DPA sections to SOC 2 controls and operational runbooks — Neha will own that and follow up early tomorrow. If you want a short walkthrough, happy to schedule a 30-minute review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie and team,

Looping in a few technical clarifications and an initial control mapping. I attached control-matrix.csv which maps DPA/DPL clauses to our SOC 2 control families and the operational runbooks where evidence lives. High level:  

- Data residency/transfer: our Hosted API routes inference tokens through region-aware endpoints; we persist minimal telemetry by default (aggregate metrics), but will disable telemetry collection for regulated customers on request. See column "persistence_note" in the CSV.
- KV cache/compute: model KV cache is ephemeral per-request and never written to durable storage. We included heap/VM-level isolation notes in the network diagram you already received.
- Subprocessors: list in the DPA annex draft includes cloud infra providers and CDN for model artifacts. We can accept customer-required subprocessors gating where we support Private deployments.

Next steps I propose: 1) I will produce a short runbook excerpt showing the audit steps we use to verify transfer paths; 2) Karthik will propose tightened DPA language for Section 4.2 (cross-border transfers).

If helpful, here is a link to the internal evidence pack (read-only): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-example-dpf-pack

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: control-matrix.csv
